turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good morning, Mr./Ms./Mrs. [Patient's Name]. I'm [Provider's Name], the anesthesiologist who will be taking care of you during your surgery today. I just need to go through a few questions to make sure we're all set for your laparoscopic cholecystectomy under general anesthesia with an LMA. Is that okay with you?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, of course. I want to make sure everything goes smoothly.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Great. Can you tell me a bit about your medical history, especially anything that might affect your anesthesia today?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Well, I have diabetes, high blood pressure, and I'm quite overweight. I take Metformin, Lisinopril, and Atorvastatin regularly. Oh, and I used to take Ranitidine for my stomach, but I stopped that a while back.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you for sharing that. I see in your records that Ranitidine is still listed as active. Can you tell me more about when and why you stopped taking it?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Oh right, I stopped taking it about six months ago. My acid reflux got better, so I didn't need it anymore. I guess I didn't update the records properly.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: That's very helpful to know. Thank you for clarifying. Do you have any allergies, and have you ever had any reactions to medications or anesthesia in the past?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, I'm allergic to penicillin. I had a rash the one time I took it. But I've never had surgery before, so no anesthesia history.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Got it. No previous anesthesia, and you're allergic to penicillin. That’s important. Now, regarding your current medications, are you taking all of them as prescribed, and have you taken them this morning?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, I took my Metformin, Lisinopril, and Atorvastatin this morning with a sip of water. I didn’t eat anything else though, since I knew I had to fast.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Perfect, thank you. And just to confirm, you’ve had nothing to eat or drink since midnight?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Correct, nothing since last night. Just a bit of water with my meds this morning.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Excellent. Now, just a few more questions. How would you describe your overall energy level and ability to walk or climb stairs? This helps us understand your fitness for surgery.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Hmm, I can walk around, but I do get a bit tired. I can’t run or anything, but I can manage daily activities. I’d say I’m moderately fit, lah.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thanks for that. It gives me a good sense of your baseline. Lastly, do you have any concerns or questions about the anesthesia or the surgery itself?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, I think I’m all set. I just want to get this done and feel better.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Great, thank you so much for going through all that with me. We’ll take good care of you today. I’ll be with you the whole time and make sure you’re comfortable and safe.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Thank you, doctor. I appreciate it.
